# Standard Set

Version 0.1.3 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

The extensions every PocketOne app has: settings, page templates, a cache, API tokens (with the OAuth server), remotes (remote/v1), MCP,
Pages, an S3 fallback bucket and S3 redirects, point-in-time restore, backups, bulk mail, deploy, WASM modules called from pb_hooks, dashboard cache headers (UI Cache), and a key-value store ($kv). Every
app uses it, standalone or an instance on a multisite host, so an app never misses one because its host forgot to
list it. Members can be reconfigured or turned off per app, never removed.

The set also gives every app's superuser dashboard PocketOne's logo and favicon, the running PocketOne version in the
footer (linked to its releases) and a Docs link to pocketone.dev/docs.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The standard set is built into `pocketone`. In your own Go build, make the app with it instead of
`pocketbase.New()`:

```go
set := standard.New()
app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
app.Start()
```

`NewApp` registers the members, loads `pb_hooks` with their JS APIs (`$mcp`, `$apiTokens`, `$bulkmail`, `$wasm`, `$llm`) and resolves
their contracts. On an app you built yourself, call `set.Register(app, jsvmConfig)` instead.

To build the app from `pocketone.yaml`'s `app` section (data folder, dev mode, hooks and migrations folders, JS engine
and its limits), load the file and pass what `AppFromConfig` returns:

```go
cfg, err := config.Load(config.FromArgs(os.Args[1:]))
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
a, err := standard.AppFromConfig(cfg)
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
app := standard.New().NewApp(a.PocketBase, a.JS)
```

Every `app` key reaches your build this way, including ones added in later releases. Your own flags override the
fields they cover.

## Configure

- **Reconfigure a member:** replace it, e.g. `set.PITR = pitr.New(pitr.Config{Retention: 7 * 24 * time.Hour})`. A
  member set to nil is an error.
- **Turn one off:** on a single app, `enabled: false` in its `pocketone.yaml` section (`api-tokens: {enabled: false}`);
  for every instance under Pocker, in its `pocker: isolate_config:` section, and for one instance, in its
  `extensions.<name>`. Extensions that require it turn off too, and
  say why. cache, storage (s3-fallback), s3redirect and pitr read `enabled` in their own sections: off, they stay registered and do nothing.
- **Keep one off in code:** a binary whose own code does what a member does sets `set.Switches`, which `Register`
  reads each member's `enabled` from (nil: `standard.ConfiguredSwitches`, the `pocketone.yaml` sections). Wrap it:
  `if name == "bulkmail" { return extkit.Config{{"enabled": false}} }; return standard.ConfiguredSwitches(name)`.
- **Add your own:** `set.Add(myextension.New())`. Extras register after the members, under the same rules.
- **Pick providers:** `set.Providers` is `pocketone.yaml`'s `providers:` section, for a contract more than one
  extension provides.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `api-tokens:`

Turns the api-tokens extension off on a single app (`enabled: false`). On a multisite host it doesn't reach the instances: use pocker's isolate_config, or an instance's `extensions.api-tokens`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false. Extensions that require it turn off too, and the startup lines say why. |

## Use

Each app logs what it got when it starts:

```
standard: on: settings, templates, cache, api-tokens, remotes, mcp, pages, storage, s3redirect, pitr, backups, bulkmail, deploy, wasm, uicache, kv, llm, llm-chat
standard: api-tokens/v1 ← api-tokens
```

With remotes off (deploy requires its remote/v1):

```
standard: remotes off: enabled: false
standard: deploy off: needs remote/v1, which nothing provides
```

## Commands and APIs

Generated from the `pocketone` binary and the contracts this extension provides.

### Commands

What it adds to the `pocketone` binary ([CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli)):

| Command | |
|---|---|
| [`pocketone cache`](/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-cache) | Shows each extension's folder in pb\_cache and its size |
| [`pocketone cache clear [extension...]`](/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-cache-clear) | Empties pb\_cache (every extension's folder, or the ones named) |
| [`pocketone extensions migrate down <extension> [n]`](/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-extensions-migrate-down) | Reverts an extension's last n migrations (default 1; 0: all of them) |
| [`pocketone extensions migrate up [extension]`](/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-extensions-migrate-up) | Applies pending extension migrations (startup does this too) |
| [`pocketone extensions migrations`](/docs/reference/cli#pocketone-extensions-migrations) | Lists each extension's migrations and whether they're applied |

## Integrations

| With | What happens |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](/docs/extensions/multisite) | Every instance that runs PocketOne gets the set. Pocker gives it to each instance (`Server.Standard`) with the instance's own `extensions.<name>` settings and the host's extras. A Docker instance on a PocketOne image runs the stock `pocketone` binary: the set with its defaults, no extras. One on a PocketBase image has none. |
| [Contracts](/docs/contracts) | Members find each other through contracts (`api-tokens/v1`), resolved per app; the startup lines show who provides what. |

## Example

```go
// A PocketOne app with the standard set and one extra extension: run it with `go run . serve`.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/jsvm"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/mailtrap"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/pitr"
	"pocketone.dev/ext/standard"
)

func main() {
	set := standard.New()
	set.PITR = pitr.New(pitr.Config{Retention: 7 * 24 * time.Hour}) // reconfigure a member
	set.Add(mailtrap.New())                                         // add your own

	app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{HooksDir: "pb_hooks"})
	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```
